children: Wheat fell below $7.20 per bushel, extending their retreat from a 3-1/2-year high of $7.67 on August 28, as traders assessed renewed diplomatic efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war.
US envoys held talks in Russia and Ukraine over the weekend, with discussions involving Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and senior European officials.
The meetings raised hopes that a potential ceasefire could help restore disrupted Black Sea grain shipments, putting additional pressure on wheat prices.
However, significant uncertainty remains, as repeated attacks by Russia and Ukraine on ports and commercial shipping sharply restricted grain exports from the region.
Although wheat supplies remain available in the Black Sea, exporters continue to face difficulties moving cargoes to international markets.
The disruption prompted Asian importers to seek alternative supplies, with trade sources reporting purchases of at least 500,000 metric tons of Australian and Argentine wheat in recent deals.

title: Wheat Eases Further from 3-1/2-Year High
